extracted.intended_audience: science journalists, researchers, and general readers interested in research integrity and science reporting
extracted.subtask_description: A news report summarizing the reasons for a journal's retraction of a published clinical trial and explaining the editorial and investigative steps taken. Useful for journalists and readers to understand standards for research reliability and how publishers handle problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about the approach to statistical analysis of the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMJ Group referred the paper to statistical experts, who identified multiple analytical errors and were unable to replicate the results. Flawed statistical approaches that prevent reproducibility are grounds for concern and can prompt retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implausible statistical values
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of implausible statistical values in the reported results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implausible or internally inconsistent statistical values signal potential errors or data problems; such values were specifically flagged in the review and contributed to the decision to retract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability/authenticity of raw data
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns about the reliability and authenticity of the raw dataset supplied by authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statisticians found irregularities in the dataset; the report concluded that data collected from each participant would require further independent scrutiny. Authenticity problems in the underlying data can justify retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate reporting of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient or inadequate reporting of methods in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete methods reporting impedes independent evaluation and replication; inadequate methodological detail was cited among the reasons leading to the retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective trial registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of prospective trial registration, breaching BMJ Group's editorial policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMJ Group noted the absence of prospective registration as a policy breach and later described the decision to publish without registration as 'the wrong decision.' Prospective registration is required by policy and its absence undermines trust in trial conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicability and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability (or inability) of independent experts to replicate the study's reported results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempts to replicate the results failed; inability to reproduce findings is a central indicator of unreliable research and may trigger formal investigation and potential retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial investigation and due process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial investigations should follow due process, involving expert review and correspondence with researchers and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMJ Group's content integrity team conducted detailed scrutiny, referred the work to external statisticians, examined correspondence, and engaged with institutions; investigations can be complex and take several months to reach a fair final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and correcting the scientific record
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers must act in the interests of openness and correct the scientific record when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors emphasized strategic, proactive investigation and the importance of transparency; retraction notices and appended expert reports are used to inform readers and prevent further citation of discredited findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' admission and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors' acknowledgment of errors and agreement to retract can be part of the resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the authors said the identified errors were honest mistakes and agreed with the decision to retract; author cooperation may influence how the issue is characterized but does not negate the need for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for journalists and others about citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and others should stop referencing or using results from studies deemed unreliable or retracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dr Helen Macdonald advised that 'journalists and others should no longer reference or use the results of this study in any future reporting.' News reports and press releases based on discredited work should be corrected or withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for high-quality evidence (clinical trials) in nutrition research
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should prioritize high-quality evidence, noting that clinical trials generally provide stronger evidence in nutritional research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor-in-chief reflected that clinical trials are prioritized as high-quality evidence though they are relatively unusual and challenging in nutrition; publishing lower-quality evidence from underrepresented environments requires extra caution.
